Subject: Clarify billing metrics for commit tiers / streaming usage

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're working the numbers for the operational budget and need a clear, contract-ready definition of how "billable usage" will be calculated for our committed hosted API tier. A few specific items our finance and procurement teams flagged: 

- When you say "billable tokens," does that include both prompt (input) + completion (output) tokens?
- For streaming responses, are tokens counted continuously as emitted, or do you aggregate into minute-level buckets for billing?
- Do you round partial tokens? If so, what's the rounding rule (round up, nearest, per-request)?
- How do you handle long-lived websocket sessions where the model is used intermittently (e.g., interactive agent sessions)?

We want to map these into a Side Letter or the Master Subscription Agreement so that the commit tiers and overage math are deterministic. If you have a short "plain English" definition + a sample billing line (example meter output for a few sample calls), that would help our legal team.

Can you also confirm whether committed thresholds (e.g., a 10M token monthly commit) are enforced per calendar month or on a 30-day rolling basis?

Attaching our draft SOW and a spreadsheet (RDW-3471-MAP-v1.xlsx) so you can see our expected traffic shape.

Best,
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Finance

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the traffic spreadsheet. I'm looping in Rishi (pricing) and Marissa (contracts) so we can give you contract-ready language. Quick, high-level answers while Rishi formats formal wording: 

- Billable tokens = input tokens + output tokens as measured by Redwood's metering logic (tokenization consistent with the model's tokenizer).
- Streaming: we meter tokens as they're emitted by the model. Billing is per token emitted; we do not bucket streaming into per-minute charges by default for hosted API.
- Rounding: we round *up* to the nearest whole token for each API call. For streaming, the same rule applies per emitted token fragment that forms a token — effectively you won't be charged fractional tokens.
- Long-lived sessions: billing is still on tokens consumed. There is no special time-based idle charge. If the session sends no tokens, there is no usage.
- Commits are handled on a calendar-month basis for hosted usage unless we agree to a 30-day rolling arrangement in the contract — happy to align to what your finance needs.

I'll let Rishi propose contract text and a sample meter output. Marissa, FYI the customer asked for explicit language about rounding and streaming; can we provide a short clause for the MSA/SLA?

Thanks — attaching an excerpt that shows "example-metering-snippets.txt" which maps a few sample calls to billable counts.

Cheers,

Vanessa / team / Emma — below is suggested contract wording plus a short explanation and a couple of negotiation levers. I've kept the clause compact so legal can drop into the MSA or Side Letter.

Suggested clause (plain text for insertion):
"Billable Usage. 'Billable Token' means a token as output by the model's canonical tokenizer and includes both tokens present in the model input (prompt) and tokens emitted in the model output (completion). For streaming responses, tokens are measured at the time they are emitted by the model and billed as consumed. Redwood rounds all fractional token measurements up to the next whole token for billing purposes. Billable usage shall be the aggregate number of Billable Tokens recorded by Redwood's metering system for the relevant billing period.

Commits and Overage. Committed Token Tiers ("Commit") are expressed as tokens per calendar month unless the parties agree in writing to a 30-day rolling measurement. If actual Billable Usage for a month exceeds the Commit for that month, overage is billed at the Overage Rate set forth in the Order Form and is not eligible for retroactive credits.

Metering and Disputes. Redwood will provide a downloadable usage CSV for the billing period showing per-request token counts, timestamps, and model variant. Customer may dispute a billing item within 45 days of invoice; if a material metering error is found by Redwood, Redwood will make a one-time adjustment as appropriate."

Explanation / negotiation points: 
- Rounding: rounding up per token is simplest operationally and caps complexity for us. Customers sometimes ask for "aggregate rounding" (round at monthly aggregate instead of per-call) — that's more favorable to the customer and could be used as a concession at larger commits.
- Streaming: measuring per emitted token is consistent with our runtime and avoids corner cases. If BrightHealth wants a separate streaming price (e.g., lower price for interactive low-latency streams), we can propose a multi-rate model: streaming tokens billed at X% of standard token rate for interactive sessions identified by route.
- Idle sessions: confirm no idle-minute charges — we've left that out, which should align with BrightHealth's ask.
- Commits window: calendar-month default is standard for hosted; we can move to 30-day rolling if procurement insists, but it complicates invoicing and forecasting.

Sample meter (excerpt):
- Call A (batch): prompt=1,230 tokens, completion=4,567 tokens => billable=5,797 tokens (rounded up per-call fragments)
- Call B (stream): emitted fragments that combine into 412.4 tokens => billable=413 tokens (rounded up)
- Long session idle: no tokens emitted => billable=0

If it helps negotiating leverage, we can offer:
- 1% reduction to the standard per-token price for a 12-month, 50M tokens/month commit (tradeoff: no aggregate-rounding concession), or
- Keep standard price but give aggregate-month rounding (rounding at the monthly total) for the first 3 months as a pilot.

Marissa / Diego: can you review the Metering and Disputes clause for any language we need to tighten on audit rights or CSV fields? Emma — happy to iterate these bullets into legal-friendly text if procurement wants specific phrasing.

Thanks,

Thanks Vanessa and Rishi — that is very helpful and much closer to what procurement needs. A couple of minor tweaks we would request before we can sign: 

1) Rounding window: instead of per-call rounding up, can we agree to "monthly aggregate rounding" (i.e., round the monthly total up to the next whole token)? That reduces overcharge noise for us and is easy to calculate on your CSV exports. If you can't do that, we'll accept per-call rounding but would like that documented as-is.

2) Commits: we prefer a 30-day rolling measurement for our cash forecasting. If you require a calendar-month default, please add an explicit option in the Order Form for 30-day rolling with an agreed invoicing cadence.

If we can agree to 1) and 2) above, procurement is OK to move forward and we'll send a countersigned Order Form. Otherwise we may need to push for those concessions in the final commercial review.

Please confirm and we can route final MSA language. Looking forward to getting this over the finish line — we like Redwood's runtime performance so far.
